Dinitrophenol is a protonophore, meaning it transports protons across membranes. This results in increased oxygen consumption. The dissipation of the proton gradient also means that ATP synthase is no longer inhibited and therefore operates at a maximal rate. This results in increased ATP production. The energy from ATP production is released as heat. Therefore, more heat is produced, but this is a result of increased ATP production, not more. The rate of NAD/NADH turnover is increased as the electron transport chain operates at a maximal rate. Thermogenin channels are only found in brown adipose tissue and are responsible for non-shivering thermogenesis. They sense the proton gradient and stimulate the release of fatty acids to be oxidised. Dinitrophenol dissipates the proton gradient and therefore has no effect on thermogenin channels. Fuel consumption is increased in all tissues as the electron transport chain operates at a maximal rate.
